results: Advanced, not settled. Kill/restart clause: in one targeted trial `bd create` was SIGKILLed 0.2 s into a call that took 0.55 s when not killed. The issue was absent afterwards, `bd list` counted only the earlier issue, and a new `bd create` on the same embedded-dolt store succeeded. Several earlier exploratory kills (0.4 s loop kills, a 0.15 s kill of a graph create) also left zero issues and a working store. The graph attempts used an invalid plan and wrote nothing. Limits: the kill timing is inferred from one unkilled baseline and was not tied to a write-in-progress signal. kill_target.log was never read. `bd doctor --check=artifacts|pollution` checks for leftover artifacts and test pollution, not store consistency, and plain `bd doctor` is unsupported in embedded mode. Companion clause ('run two companion review sessions in one workspace, interrupt one'): not attempted. Blocker: it needs two concurrent Claude Code sessions each driving the Codex companion. The unit rules defer multi-session Claude use while the shared Claude account is reserved, and limit the unit to at most one concurrent Codex call. A temp HOME, `unshare` or a loopback-only instance does not change either limit, because both are account and concurrency rules, not host state.
limits: One targeted kill trial on a scratch single-writer store; no write-activity signal at the kill; no store-consistency checker available in embedded mode. Companion concurrent/interrupted-review clause blocked by the Claude-account reservation and the one-concurrent-Codex-call rule. Raw outputs: raw/gap8-transcript-extract.json.
